title: Internal Structure of Molecular Gas in a Main-sequence Galaxy With a UV Clump at z = 1.45
question: Internal distribution and properties of molecular gas (CO(2-1), CO(5-4), R52 ratio, rotation, gas fraction profile) in a massive main-sequence galaxy with a UV clump at z = 1.45, compared with the stellar distribution

data.angular_resolution: CO(2-1): ~0.55 arcsec; CO(5-4): ~0.7 arcsec (as stated for the observations)
data.sensitivity: 0.18 mJy/beam (CO(2-1)) and 0.91 mJy/beam (CO(5-4)) per 25 km/s channel

what.value: Stellar mass (SED fitting, Bruzual03 models, Salpeter IMF corrected with factor 0.58) and SFR from rest-UV luminosity for SXDS1_13015

evidence.quote: The stellar masses were derived by spectral energy distribution (SED) fittings with optical to mid-infrared data, adopting the stellar population synthesis model by (cite: Bruzual03) and the IMF by (cite: Salpeter55).
After correcting the difference of the adopted IMF with the factor of 0.58 (cite: Speagle14)

external_data.citation: Yabe12 (cite: Yabe12); Speagle14 (cite: Speagle14) for the IMF factor

what.value: Gas-phase metallicity 12+log(O/H) = 8.85 from the N2 method (Pettini04 calibration)

evidence.quote: the gas metallicities were derived based on N2 method (cite: Pettini04)

what.value: Metallicity-dependent CO-to-H2 conversion factor, Equation (7) of Genzel15

evidence.loc: 4.1.1 Total Flux and Molecular Gas Mass
evidence.quote: we adopt the Equation (7) of (cite: Genzel15)

what.value: CO(5-4) ALMA Cycle 0 data and its calibration (CASA 4.2)

evidence.quote: The raw visibility data of CO(5-4) was calibrated with CASA version 4.2 by (cite: Seko16).

what.value: Median stellar mass surface density profiles of galaxies at different redshifts for comparison

evidence.quote: the derived profile of SXDS1_13015 is plotted with the median profiles of galaxies at different redshifts by (cite: Patel13)

what.value: CO and optical half-light radii of field main-sequence and sBzK galaxies

evidence.quote: The field sample includes 12 main sequence galaxies at $z \sim 1 - 1.5$ by (cite: Tacconi13) and 3 sBzK galaxies by (cite: Daddi10).

what.value: CO and optical half-light radii of 4 cluster galaxies at z ~ 1.6

evidence.quote: The cluster sample consists of 4 cluster galaxies at $z \sim 1.6$ by (cite: Noble19)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image the CO cubes
recipe.method: Calibrate with observatory script (CO(2-1)) and Seko16 calibration (CO(5-4)); continuum-subtract CO(5-4) with uvcontsub; 3 sigma-clean tclean channel maps at 25 km/s
key_parameters: Briggs weighting robust = 0.5; channel width 25 km/s

recipe.goal: Measure total CO(2-1) and CO(5-4) fluxes
recipe.method: Fit an elliptical Gaussian to the integrated intensity maps within a 1.5 arcsec diameter circle centred on the CO(2-1) peak

recipe.goal: Derive CO(1-0) luminosity, molecular gas mass, gas fraction and depletion time
recipe.method: L'CO(1-0) from CO(2-1) flux with R21 = 2; M_mol = alpha_CO L'CO(1-0) with metallicity-dependent alpha_CO; f_gas = M_mol/(M_mol+M_star); depletion time = M_mol/SFR
key_parameters: alpha_CO from Equation (7) of Genzel15 using 12+log(O/H) on the Pettini04 scale
assumptions: R21 = CO(2-1)/CO(1-0) flux ratio of 2 (Milky Way like)
alpha_CO includes a 36% mass contribution of helium
Flat cosmology with Omega_M = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7, H0 = 70 km/s/Mpc; Chabrier IMF

recipe.method: Divide CO(5-4) 0th moment map by CO(2-1) map convolved to the CO(5-4) beam, in pixels with S/N > 2.5 in CO(5-4)
key_parameters: S/N > 2.5 threshold in the CO(5-4) map; also a map in the velocity range -250 to 0 km/s

recipe.goal: Test significance of CO(5-4) peak offset and velocity shift; align HST to ALMA
recipe.method: Simulate CO(5-4) observations with simobserve of a Gaussian mimicking the CO(5-4) distribution and line profile to get 1-sigma uncertainties on peak position and velocity; shift HST astrometry assuming the J125 peak coincides with the CO(2-1) moment-0 peak
assumptions: J125 peak coincides with CO(2-1) peak because CO(2-1) has a symmetric profile and high S/N

recipe.goal: Fit a rotating disk to the CO(2-1) cube
recipe.method: GalPaK3D disk model (exponential flux profile n=1, hyperbolic tangent rotation curve) convolved with PSF and LSF fit to the CO(2-1) channel cube; uncertainties from 100 simulated cubes with random noise seeds, combined in quadrature with systematic error
key_parameters: PSF = synthesized beam 0.61 x 0.53 arcsec, PA = 79 deg; LSF = 25 km/s channel
Free parameters: central position, central frequency, total flux, r1/2, inclination, PA, turnover radius, Vmax, constant sigma0
assumptions: Velocity dispersion constant over the disk; sigma0 poorly constrained because of beam smearing

recipe.goal: Fit Sersic models to HST J125 and H160 images
recipe.method: GALFIT single-component Sersic fit and two-component fit with bulge n=4 and disk n=1 (disk position, PA and axis ratio fixed to the single-component values) in a ~2.5 x 2.5 arcsec region with PSFs from stacked stars
key_parameters: PSF from stacking four (J125) or six (H160) unsaturated stars; ~2.5 x 2.5 arcsec boxy fitting region; neighbours masked
assumptions: Bulge n=4 and disk n=1 fixed because the galaxy has a rotating gas disk and appears to have a bulge and disk in HST

recipe.goal: Compare gas and stellar radial profiles, f_gas(r) and dynamical masses
recipe.method: Combine GalPaK3D gas model and GALFIT stellar model into intrinsic radial surface profiles and f_gas at each radius; Mdyn(r) ~ r v_rot^2 / G at r1/2, 2 r1/2, 3 r1/2; inner gas and stellar masses scaled by J125 luminosity within r
assumptions: Constant mass-to-luminosity ratio for the stellar mass surface density

recipe.goal: Compare CO and optical half-light radii with literature samples
recipe.method: Place the target on the optical versus CO half-light radius plane with field and cluster galaxies at z ~ 1-1.6 from the literature

score_reason: Both projects are named and a good part of the recipe is given (CASA versions, robust, channel width, GalPaK3D and GALFIT set-up, numeric tables), but imaging masks, line-free channels, fitting priors and the CO(5-4) calibration (in Seko16) are missing, and the R21 value is internally inconsistent
rediscovery_reason: ALMA Cycle 0 and Cycle 3 data of named projects are normally in the public archive, the key results (fluxes, R52, GalPaK3D parameters, f_gas) are numeric, and the recipe is mostly complete, although the paper does not itself state public availability
